blinding_compliance: I reviewed only the supplied blind packet and public technical knowledge; I did not inspect the repository outside this item, coordinator directory, hidden truth files, scoring code, other reviewer outputs, or search the benchmark/paper name.
ai_assistance: AI assistant used to draft this review output from the supplied packet.

forbidden_at_checkpoint: Treating the roughness readings as adequate for specification-conformance or pass/fail decisions: %Tolerance=43.92% (>30%) and ndc=5 mean the gage cannot reliably classify borderline parts against 0.40-1.60 um Ra.
Asserting Cp/Cpk/Pp/Ppk and the out-of-spec count as valid process-capability/conformance conclusions without first improving the gage or correcting for measurement variance.
Concluding that the single 1.64 um Ra bore is definitely out of spec given the gage error relative to the 0.04 um excess above the 1.60 upper limit.
Concluding that the true process mean is 0.109 um Ra above target or that a 0.11 um Ra recentering shift is a validated required adjustment, since no gage accuracy/bias/linearity study was reported.

Calling the statistically significant operator effect an 'operator bias' and recommending operator-alignment correction as an established improvement: the ANOVA operator effect is a reproducibility effect, not bias against a reference standard.
permitted_at_checkpoint: Reporting the gage R&R estimates themselves and stating that the system is marginal for monitoring but unacceptable for tolerance-based conformance decisions.
Descriptive summaries of the 50-bore run, including mean, median, standard deviation, and normality, clearly labelled as observed readings that include measurement error.
An I-MR chart and runs test in finishing order as exploratory screening only, with limits understood to be widened by measurement error and not proof of true process stability.
Planning a gage improvement, calibration, or accuracy/bias study before any pass/fail, capability, or recentering decision.
Forming a recentering hypothesis for later testing after the measurement system is improved or measurement variance is explicitly corrected.
forbidden_quotes: Readings can carry the conclusions below; a later gage improvement (operator bias, p ≈ 5.0e-6) would tighten borderline calls.
The process was in statistical control for the whole run. Its behaviour is a steady, common-cause system sitting above target.
1 of 50 bores was out of spec: 1.64 um Ra vs the 1.60 upper limit.
Recenter the process to the 1.00 target. The required shift is about 0.11 um Ra of mean.
reviews.extra_computation_detail: The descriptive summary, normality check, I-MR chart, and runs test are acceptable only as exploratory screening of observed readings. The capability analysis and out-of-spec classification are unacceptable because the measurement system has %Tolerance=43.92% and no accuracy/bias study, so conformance/capability conclusions are not supported; the report relied on them rather than merely describing them with use withheld.
allowed_alternatives: Use the I-MR chart and runs test only as exploratory monitoring of observed readings, with widened limits and no specification-conformance or capability conclusions.
Before capability analysis, improve the gage to %Tolerance<=30% and ndc>=5 and then recompute Cp/Cpk/Pp/Ppk.
Alternatively, use the MSA variance components to report measurement-corrected capability with explicit assumptions, and avoid reporting raw out-of-spec counts as definitive.
For pass/fail use, perform a gage accuracy/bias/linearity study first, then use guard-banding or re-measure borderline units with a better system.
Run an accuracy/bias study before concluding the process mean is above target and before recommending a quantitative recentering shift.
evidence: Gage R&R outputs: %StudyVariation=25.69%, %Tolerance=43.92%, ndc=5, operator p≈5.0e-6, interaction p=0.679.
Capability outputs: Cp=1.042, Cpk=0.853, Pp=1.023, Ppk=0.837, out-of-spec count=1.
Report caveat: 'The high %Tolerance (43.92%) reflects that the 10 study bores spanned almost the whole band; for pass/fail decisions near a limit the measurement error is not negligible.'
Report assertion: 'Readings can carry the conclusions below; a later gage improvement (operator bias, p ≈ 5.0e-6) would tighten borderline calls.'
Report assertion: '1 of 50 bores was out of spec: 1.64 um Ra vs the 1.60 upper limit.'
reviews.rationale: The gage R&R results do not support tolerance-based conformance or capability conclusions: %Tolerance is above the usual 30% limit, ndc is only 5, and only precision was studied, not accuracy/bias. The report's own caveat admits the measurement error is not negligible near limits, but then it asserts capability indices, an out-of-spec bore, and a quantitative recentering recommendation. Descriptive and exploratory monitoring can continue, but the focal substantive advancement should be paused until the gage is improved or measurement variance is explicitly corrected.
reviews.numerical_check: Self-report-only for raw data; checked internal arithmetic from reported stdDev and MRbar: Pp=1.2/(6*0.19548)=1.023; Cp=1.2/(6*(0.21653/1.128))=1.042; Cpk/Ppk match the reported mean and limits.
reviews.evidence_problem: No raw MSA or process-run data were supplied in this packet; self-report-only. No gage accuracy, bias, linearity, or calibration study was reported.
